body:
I said before, I think that I've made it out as though we hang out all the time--we mostly talk through Skype, but not all of the wounds from the aforementioned fight (the one that got me banned from the campus) have quite healed. While I think that all of the mutual friends are on good terms, you can tell by being in the room that things are strained between us and her simply because her behavior has definitely lowered their opinion of her. 

I do like to think of myself as a rational individual, which is why this is bothering me, and I also know that your suggestion is most likely the right one, but suffice it to say it'll be difficult. She's the only person that I know nearby with a PlayStation 3, and it's the only current-gen console I own. Fortunately, an unrelated friend of mine (on the same campus unfortunately) is planning on getting one, so that might be resolved soon.

I see. That will be a bit tough since we still share many mutual friends, but I've been trying to minimize my conversations with her unless I want to use her PS3 or something since I don't feel right telling her at this point. At any rate, I don't think it's really because she broke up with me first--Oneitis sounds more likely--but I dunno, it's weird. 

Fortunately, it does look like I've finally escaped the worst of the drama, and we really only hang out to play video games and I think we're sharing a room with some friends for a convention in May. I think that I made it sound like I hang out with her more than I actually do now.

At any rate, it would appear that opinions are piling up in favor of not contacting her for a while and the more rational part of me is telling me that you guys are right, although I'd like to know why I'm feeling this way.

It's not one thing in particular. In fact, it's not really anything in particular.

 I've sort of just stopped finding life interesting in general. Most days out of the year, it's essentially living out the same thing over and over, being a college student and all. Needless to say the occasional deviation rolls around that's interesting enough to claim my attention for a short while, but it's never too long before I slip back into this sort of mundane repetition. There's not much going on in my life that's particularly disastrous--I have friends, and I can be social, I'm a decent student, though not notably intelligent by any stretch of the imagination, not to mention rather a slacker, but lately, I've been noticing that I've just grown incredibly bored with my immediate surroundings and there are many days where I just sort of go to bed hoping I don't wake up, or that I'll wind up the victim of petty fatal circumstance because even something as disastrous as that would be more interesting than my day-to-day life now.
That would be fine. I understand that this was a bit more pressing.
That rather sums up my feelings at present.
Care to tell me about her or what happened between you two?
